requirement:
By default, authoring MUST suppress per-subject `true` judgment lines and show
each `false` judgment's subject and outcome on stderr, on both terminals and
redirected output. Existing progress counters and completion summaries MUST remain
available; FIXME notices and authoring errors MUST remain visible. Single-subject
authoring MUST retain its subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and
usage-record metadata.

`-v` and `--verbose` MUST additionally show each false judgment's recorded Markdown
rationale on stderr; rationales MUST be omitted by default. This applies to
single-subject and batch authoring. It MUST
NOT print true rationales or append recorded
input snapshots. Reporting MUST use the completed assessment's existing result,
without additional inference. In `--stdout` mode, stdout MUST remain only the
evidence JSON; verbose rationale and other diagnostics MUST go to stderr.
Verbosity MUST NOT change persistence, validation, or exit-status rules.

rationale:
I found no gap. Each obligation maps to code reachable from the `{impl}` item `fn main` in `src/main.rs`, and each has a test that carries a `{test}` reference.

**Batch reporting** (`run_batch` in `src/authoring/batch.rs`, reached from `main` via `author_all_with_options`; reporting is done by `BatchProgress` in `src/authoring/progress.rs`)
- **Suppress `true` lines:** `BatchProgress::completed` increments the counter for a `true` judgment and prints nothing.
- **Show `false` subject and outcome on stderr:** it prints `"{subject}: false (usage: …)"` through `println`. That goes to `bar.println` on a terminal and `eprintln!` when redirected, so both cases are covered.
- **Rationale only with `-v`/`--verbose`:** the rationale is appended only when `self.verbose` is set. It comes from `assessment.rationale`, which is the record's rationale, so no new inference runs. `true` rationales are never printed, and no input snapshots are printed.
- **FIXME and errors stay visible:** `completed` prints `"{subject}: FIXME (usage: …)"` and `failed` prints `"{label}: {error}"`.
- **Counters and summary remain:** `refresh` and `start` draw the progress counters, and `main` prints the final `"N authored; …"` summary line to stdout.
- **Verbosity changes nothing else:** `verbose` only reaches `BatchProgress`. `AuthoringOptions.verbose` has no other use, so persistence, validation and exit status are untouched.

**Single-subject reporting** (`main`, `Command::Author`)
- **Summary line:** it prints subject, backend, model and policy, with ` — FIXME` appended for a FIXME judgment.
- **`false` handling:** for a `false` judgment it calls `eprintln!("{subject}: false")` and, only under `verbose`, `eprintln!` of the rationale.
- **Destination and usage record:** it prints the evidence path and usage path to stdout in file mode, or `Evidence: stdout` and the usage path to stderr in stdout mode.
- **Stdout mode:** stdout carries only the evidence JSON, written in `configured_assessment` in `src/authoring/mod.rs`. In stdout mode no replaced record is read, so no coverage-loss output goes to stdout.
- **No extra inference:** `author_evidence_with_options` makes one assessment, and reporting reuses its outcome.

**Tests**
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs::batch_reports_false_rationales_only_when_verbose` runs redirected output with and without `--verbose`. It checks:
  - the `false` line is present and no `true` line appears;
  - the rationale appears only under `--verbose`;
  - the FIXME line and the error are visible;
  - no `true` rationale or source snapshot is printed;
  - the stdout summary is unchanged.
- `terminal_progress_distinguishes_judgments_from_authoring_errors` runs in a pty and checks the progress counters, the `false` and FIXME lines, no `true` line, and the error text.
- `verbose_false_rationale_is_readable_above_terminal_progress` runs `-v` in a pty.
- `failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure` checks the nonzero exit status and the visible error.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs::verbose_single_author_reports_only_false_rationale_without_source_inputs` covers `-v` and `--verbose` for a `false` judgment and `-v` for a `true` one. It checks:
  - the rationale is printed only for `false`;
  - `true` lines and source or definition text are absent;
  - `Evidence:` and `Usage:` are present;
  - evidence is persisted and the exit status is success;
  - the model server receives exactly one request.
- `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` covers stdout mode with and without verbose, for `true`, `false` and FIXME. It checks:
  - stdout is parseable JSON only;
  - stderr has the subject, backend/model, `Evidence: stdout` and the usage path;
  - the rationale appears only for verbose `false`;
  - project files are unchanged.
- `false_is_a_completed_assessment` checks that the `false` line goes to stderr and not stdout, and that the rationale is hidden by default.

None of the code paths is untested or lacks a `{test}` reference.

:::{req} invocation
`habeas author <full-name> [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [--stdout] [-v|--verbose]`
MUST author the evidence of one existing requirement or named example in the
current project, under {cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`. It MUST report the
selected subject, backend, model, evidence destination, and usage-record path on
completion. The evidence destination MUST identify the evidence-file path by
default or stdout when `--stdout` is selected. In stdout mode, the completion
report and diagnostics MUST go to stderr. `author-evidence` MUST remain an alias
for the single-subject command.
:::{req} batch
`habeas author --all [--config <name>] [--missing | --force] [-v|--verbose]` MUST author
the evidence of every current requirement and named example, together with the
reviews {cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and
{cite}`requirements.references.site_review` include, under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.refresh`.
`--all` MUST be mutually exclusive with a subject name and `--stdout`. It MUST
also delete each orphaned citation review under
{cite}`requirements.references.citation_review` and each orphaned site review
under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and report each deletion; the
deletion MUST NOT require model configuration or credentials.
Failure to discover declarations or to read, scan, or parse project sources MUST report an error,
not a successful empty batch.
Each subject MUST receive an independent assessment with its own prompt, inputs,
judgment, and usage record. The command MUST report aggregate completion and each
authoring error under {cite}`requirements.authoring.reporting`, and retain
successful writes when another assessment fails. It MUST return a nonzero
exit status if any assessment fails. False judgments MUST still be written as
completed assessments; they remain failures under ordinary evidence validation.
An access-policy denial MUST abort only the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.read_denial`. Interruption MUST instead stop the
whole batch: queued assessments MUST NOT start, running assessments MUST be
cancelled, and an assessment whose evidence has not been written when the
interruption arrives MUST NOT write it. Evidence already written MUST be
retained, and the command MUST report the number of assessments not started as
a batch failure.
The bundled Habeas skills MUST direct the supervising agent to run this command
to create or refresh evidence. They MUST leave judgments, rationales, and input
snapshots to the authoring harness; the supervising agent addresses findings by
changing requirements, source citations, implementation, or tests.
